method.selected_fault: One SIGKILL 9 through the held original watchdog pidfd after the ordinary observer published a bound READY record; the owner, original service, client, parent and grandchild were live immediately before the signal.
method.identity_method: The frozen actor required a singleton original service task list, exactly three original service direct children, a unique root-owned watchdog in the service supervisor subgroup, matching service executable and start identity, a service-held pidfd targeting that watchdog, and a matching external held pidfd. It rechecked the identity immediately before the signal.

observed.first_original_client_completion_sample: Retained original service, parent, intermediate, grandchild and watchdog pidfds were terminal with fdinfo Pid=-1; the original domain was empty or retired. These were sequential observations before fixture assistance.
observed.manager_result: Original unit failed with ExecMainCode=1, ExecMainStatus=125 and Result=exit-code; MainPID and ControlPID were zero.
observed.transport_stderr: A separate 72-byte pseudo-terminal allocation notice was retained; the product client diagnostic is the 53-byte stderr above.

prior_preparation.watchdog_packet_002: Local namespace admission failed before SSH or product execution; preserved as a failure.
prior_preparation.watchdog_packet_003: Local READY mock admission failed before SSH or product execution; preserved as a failure.
prior_preparation.watchdog_packet_004_first_local_verifier: A first local verifier requested the wrong sealed-result filename and failed before SSH or product execution. The corrected verifier passed without rerunning the sealed mock results.

qualification_limits: The external first-completion observation supports safety settlement for this one selected fault. The product returned a native-quarantine diagnostic; it did not report native-verified settlement.

The internal native stop and cancellation bits were not exported. This case does not prove that the watchdog-only classifier branch ran or that the watchdog was the exclusive causal reason for client exit 125.

The first client, held pidfd and domain readings are sequential samples, not one atomic kernel snapshot; they do not prove exact kernel exit ordering. Systemd control-group handling may contribute to descendant termination.

The frozen actor read and required a singleton service task list twice, but the raw task names were not serialized separately; this public summary does not claim independent raw reconstruction of that list.
The observed actor recorded a successful held-watchdog signal call; no separate kernel trace was captured.
Retained private source, raw captures and receipts support this summary. A complete public reproduction package is not provided.
This single case does not qualify the full Linux backend, default dispatch, or performance; no primary competitive performance measurement was taken.
